independentReview.head: e02b24decfff994e5013293500197f372aaad12e
independentReview.reason: FIRST PASS - FIX-BEFORE-MERGE on a confirmed logic defect, and it was a real one: incident_id is a hash over the crash's traits INCLUDING its instant, and blackbox::merge_into moves that instant - and fills in the faulting module - the moment a corroborating WER report lands. So one crash wears two ids across two scans, the second id reads as never-seen, and a card the user had just DISMISSED is announced again, breaking the module's own stated no-reannounce contract. Fixed by recording each row's matching traits at observation time and reconciling shifted identities before anything decides what is new, gated on the old id having left the report so two genuinely-live ids stay two incidents. Its second warning (a lost-update TOCTOU on the state file, and a shared temp filename) is fixed by one process lock around every read-modify-write plus a per-call temp path. Its guard-weakness note is fixed too: the trigger-wiring check now reads comment-stripped source, so a '// TODO: wire ScanTrigger::Foreground' can no longer satisfy it. Every one of the three is pinned by a new regression test before the fix was counted, per bug->guard. SECOND PASS - CLEAN at this head, and not by re-reading its own prior notes: it re-ran cargo test --lib (1155 passed), clippy -D warnings, vitest on the contract file plus adjacent surfaces (81 + 122 passed) and tsc --noEmit in this worktree, then confirmed each of the three fixes by hand-tracing rather than by assertion count - including that two_ids_that_are_both_live_stay_two_incidents is NOT vacuous (its 40s gap sits inside blackbox::CROSS_SOURCE_WINDOW_SECS, so the test exercises the live-gate itself), that adopt() preserves dismissed_at by construction because it mutates the same row, that one stale row cannot adopt two live incidents because live() is re-evaluated per iteration, and that ScanClaim's Drop still fires on the throttle-check early return. It re-verified all six hard constraints independently plus the four-authority command surface, and judged staying at SCHEMA_VERSION 1 correct because the three new fields are additive under serde(default) and an old file loads rather than quarantining. ITS ONE NIT IS ACCEPTED, NOT WAIVED, and deliberately not taken in this PR: src/care-incident-observer-contract.test.ts:139 lets the should_scan throttle-check match either 'state.last_scan_at' or 'read_state().last_scan_at', and only the second reads through the lock - so the guard would also accept a regression back to the unlocked read it exists to catch. It is guard precision, not a production defect (the sole call site is the locked one). Taking it here would move the head off the one this review covers and force a third review round for a test-only regex; it lands instead in the post-merge commit on main, in the same change that retires this lane's disposition row. The frontend auditor separately confirmed the Tauri camelCase arg convention across the three new commands (its own top suspect) and returned clean on types, locales and prop threading; its two nits - a duplicate mount-time invoke, and a stale selection surviving a manual station reopen - were both fixed rather than waved off.
